reasons: No test or other evidence is visible.
Errors are caught and shown with a message.
Progress is shown in fixed steps rather than real transfer progress.

terms.meaning: A temporary web address that lets a file be sent straight to storage without a separate login.
A web request that sends data to an address.
A file upload library that many apps use to manage uploads.
The stored location of the uploaded file.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports
sections.what: Brings in state and callback tools, plus the Uppy file type.
sections.why: Needed for the hook's state and for typing the second upload path.
sections.watch_out: Uppy is only used as a type here, so it is not loaded at run time.

sections.name: UploadMetadata
sections.title: Metadata shape
sections.what: Describes the basic file details sent to the server: name, size and type.
sections.why: Likely reason: these are what the server needs to issue an address. Otherwise reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The field names must match what the server expects.

sections.name: UploadResponse
sections.title: Server reply shape
sections.what: Describes what the server returns: the address to send the file to, the stored path and the metadata.
sections.why: Gives callers the stored path to keep.
sections.watch_out: The field names must match the server exactly, or the upload fails.

sections.name: UseUploadOptions
sections.title: Callback options
sections.what: Describes two optional callbacks: one runs on success and receives the reply, the other runs on error and receives the error.
sections.why: Lets callers react to the result without the hook managing their screens.
sections.watch_out: Both are optional. A caller that ignores errors gets no message from the callbacks, although the hook's error state still holds one.

sections.name: useUpload (part 1)
sections.title: Hook state and address request
sections.what: Starts the hook with flags for in progress, error and progress. Includes the usage notes. Defines the first step, which asks the server for an upload address.
sections.why: Splitting the steps keeps the server request separate from sending the file.
sections.watch_out: The request sends only the file's details, never the file itself.

sections.name: useUpload: async
sections.title: Sending the file to the address
sections.what: Sends the file with a PUT request to the address, and checks the result. A failed reply raises an error.
sections.why: This is the second step, where the file goes directly to storage.
sections.watch_out: A mismatch between the content type sent and the type used when the address was issued can cause storage to refuse the file.

sections.name: useUpload: async
sections.title: Full upload run
sections.what: Runs the whole upload: resets state, requests the address, sends the file, moves progress through fixed steps, and then calls success or error. Also begins the Uppy version, which requests an address for each file.
sections.why: The code comments name each step. The reason for fixed steps is not stated.
sections.watch_out: Progress jumps in fixed steps, so the percentage does not show real transfer speed.

sections.name: useUpload (part 4)
sections.title: Uppy parameters and return value
sections.what: Gives the Uppy plugin the method, address and content type it needs. Ends by returning the functions and state that screens use.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets Uppy upload directly without a separate step in the screen.
sections.watch_out: This path has its own request and error message, so a change to one must be checked against the other.

summary: A hook that uploads a file in two steps: it asks the server for a temporary upload address, then sends the file straight to that address.
purpose: Lets screens upload files, such as documents, into storage without sending the file through the app's own server.
why: The header comment describes the two-step design. Sending only details first keeps the file itself off the app server. Otherwise the reason is not stated in the code.
how: Holds upload state: in progress, error and a progress number. The uploadFile function asks the server for an address using the file's name, size and type. It then sends the file with a PUT request, updates the progress, and calls the success or error callback. A second function, getUploadParameters, does the same steps in the format the Uppy upload library expects.
inputs: A File from an input element, or an Uppy file for the second path. Optional success and error callbacks.
outputs: uploadFile returns the upload result, or null on error, plus flags for in progress, error and progress. getUploadParameters returns a method, an address and headers.
risks: Progress moves in fixed steps, not real bytes sent. Both paths call the same server address. The options object is in a memo key, so a new object each render recreates the function. Requests here add no authorization header, so the server must accept them or a global setup must add one.
debug: If an upload fails at the start, check the request-url endpoint and the message it returns. If it fails at the storage step, check the address and content type. Progress that seems stuck at fixed steps is expected.
